name: Huntington University
academic_ranking: Private Christian liberal arts university founded in 1897, affiliated with the Church of the United Brethren in Christ and a member of the CCCU. Consistently recognized among the best regional universities in the Midwest by U.S. News & World Report, Forbes, and The Princeton Review. No exact numeric ranking captured from official source.
financial_aid: 100% of traditional full-time HU students receive financial aid. The university offers 143 different scholarships and awarded roughly $17 million in aid for 2025/2026. Aid types include academic, athletic, performance, department, and need-based awards, plus alumni/church-service awards. Additional sources include federal aid (up to $7,395 for 25/26), Indiana State grants (up to $10,600 for 25/26), loans, and work-study. Source: huntington.edu/financial-aid, checked 2026-07.
facilities_notes: Softball plays at the HU Softball Field on the Huntington campus. Athletics facilities also include the Merillat Physical Education & Recreation Complex (weight/exercise rooms, Platt Arena), Forest Glen Park, King Stadium, and other venues. Source: huathletics.com/facility, checked 2026-07.
program_reputation: NAIA member competing in the Crossroads League. Part of Huntington University's 18-sport athletics program (Foresters). Detailed competitive-history notes not captured from official source.
notes: Athletics site: huathletics.com (Sidearm/PrestoSports; returns 403 to some automated fetchers, retrieved via browser user agent). Softball program pages under /sports/sball/. Roster size (28) counted from unique player bios on the 2025-26 softball roster (huathletics.com/sports/sball/2025-26/roster); the 2026-27 roster was not yet populated at time of research.
